title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-09-20
lineage: SBD > MR > 7inch Reel (2nd Gen) > Revox A-77 Alesis Masterlink ML-9600 (24/96) > CDR (16/44.1) > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with noticeable hiss and occasional level distortion, but a stellar late‑'70 show highlighted by a soaring acoustic set and monster Not Fade Away jam.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised – the acoustic set (Working Man’s Dead, Uncle John’s Band, Ripple, Lay Me Down) is called “divine,” and the electric second set delivers a thunderous Not Fade Away > Caution/Feedback sequence plus an unforgettable Easy Wind.  Technically the tape suffers from hiss, occasional over‑driven levels (especially on Caution), and some drop‑outs, but most listeners deem it acceptable for a 1970 SBD and prefer its raw detail over cleaner remasters.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviewers (≈70 %) give 4‑5 stars, emphasizing the show’s musical brilliance despite consistent complaints about hiss and occasional distortion.  Show quality dominates the rating, with recording flaws lowering it only slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mixed‑source SBD with pervasive tape hiss, level spikes that cause distortion (notably on Caution/Feedback), occasional drop‑outs and uneven balance.  Still considered listenable and “good for its age” by most.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A lush acoustic set opens the night, highlighted by guest mandolin and tight vocal harmonies, then flips into a high‑energy electric second set where Not Fade Away rolls straight into a wild Caution/Feedback jam and an epic Easy Wind.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as solid and “at the helm,” with crisp guitars despite tape hiss.
band_member_comments.Bob: His solo on Easy Wind is specifically praised.
band_member_comments.Keys: Mentions of piano/organ (likely Pigpen) and a guest mandolin that adds depth to the acoustic set.
